candidate.answerReason: Any divisor producing equal remainders must divide both consecutive differences, 392 and 686. Their greatest common factor is 98, and division by 98 gives remainder 85 for all three numbers.

methods.label: Subtract to cancel the remainder
methods.explanation:
Equal remainders disappear when we subtract the numbers. Thus, if the positive integer \(d\) leaves the same remainder in all three divisions, it must divide
\[
13{,}903-13{,}511=392
\]
and
\[
14{,}589-13{,}903=686.
\]
It must therefore also divide
\[
2(392)-686=98.
\]
Consequently, \(d\leq 98\).

To show that this bound is attained, write
\[
\begin{aligned}
13{,}511&=98(137)+85,\\
13{,}903&=98(141)+85,\\
14{,}589&=98(148)+85.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(0\leq85<98\), these are valid divisions with the same remainder. The greatest divisor is therefore \(\boxed{98}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The proof uses elementary divisibility, subtraction, and a direct greatest-common-factor argument.
